title: Swan Race · Schlupfwerk
summary: As Founder & Game Developer of Schlupfwerk, my indie game studio, I make Swan Race: a free, open-source 3D racing game for the whole family, built with Godot. The Windows alpha is already out.
highlights: The track, scenery, characters and music are generated in code: on top of the Godot engine, the game takes about 200 KB.
The 11 rivals are AI bots that produce the same commands as a player and follow the same physics, no cheating; the difficulty draws each one's skill.
A version tag triggers GitHub Actions, which exports the game, packages the zip with the licenses and publishes the release.

title: ERP Mock · WPF + API
summary: A mini-ERP for customers, products, sales that draw down stock, a dashboard and reports. The business rules live in an HTTP API and WPF is just the interface.
highlights: The WPF app and the tests use the same HTTP client, which implements the service interfaces: the screens didn’t change when the rules moved to the API.
A business-rule error (not enough stock, invalid tax ID) comes back as a 422 ProblemDetails and shows up as-is on screen.
Four ADRs record the decisions, from splitting out the API to PostgreSQL in Docker with SQLite as the local default.

title: Loja Mock · a Selenium lab
summary: An online store in React, fully mocked with no backend, built for practicing test automation: login, catalog, cart with coupons, checkout, orders and sign-up, in mobile mode too.
highlights: Every interactive element has a data-testid, so test selectors don’t break when the layout changes.
URL flags wipe the data (?reset=1) and set the simulated latency (?delay=), for practicing explicit waits.
Error cases on purpose: a blocked user, an expired coupon, a declined card, an out-of-stock product.

title: Assistente Chat · Alexa + Claude
summary: A Brazilian Portuguese Alexa skill that sends your spoken question to the Claude API and reads the answer out loud, like a built-in Alexa command.
highlights: Alexa waits about 8 s for an answer: hence a fast model, a 7 s timeout and short answers with no markdown.
The answer is cleaned up and escaped for SSML before it becomes speech.
The API key never goes into Git; a script builds the zip to import into the Alexa console.

title: SQLite Merge Tool
summary: A Windows tool that copies table data between two SQLite databases, replacing the destination rows or adding to them. Built in 2016 for a day-to-day need, written by hand, before AI coding assistants.
highlights: The UI only handles screens and threads; all database work lives in a separate Core library.
In 2026 it was made to build again and got docs and ADRs, and it stays on .NET Framework 4.8 on purpose, as a record of my journey.
